title: runtime feedback pocket synthesis — deployment & probe lanes (Aug 2026)
content:
Purpose
---
Quick pocket synthesis of recent customer feedback (pilot + top-tier customers) focused on runtime friction that is driving support tickets and feature asks. Goal: surface highest-leverage probe lanes we can run in the next 4–6 weeks and a small set of low-effort patches that unblock customers or reduce ops load. This is intentionally lightweight — think: field notes + recommended next steps.

Input sources
- 18 support threads (June–Aug 2026) tagged "latency-regression" and "kv-cache".
- Two Dedicated pilots (FinSaaS, MedScan) weekly calls + telemetry exports.
- Internal SRE incident postmortem (INC-2026-07-18) re: unexpected tail latency spike.
- Small UX interviews (3 customers) around model selection and quantization messaging.

Topline signals (tl;dr)
- Latency tail events remain the #1 pain for high-throughput customers; when tails appear they correlate with cache misses + warmup on longer-sequence requests.
- KV prefix caching is delivering clear cost wins but customers lack visibility and controls to reason about cache effectiveness per-route. Requests: per-route cache hit rate, evict-by-tag, and TTL control.
- Quantization guidance inside the Console is confusing: customers want concrete tradeoffs (latency vs quality) by workload, not generic model-level recommendations.
- Small but recurrent ask for an explicit fallback policy UI: e.g., automatically route to the smaller/quantized variant under capacity constraints with visible audit trail.

Representative customer quotes
- "We had a 3x token cost spike in the morning and couldn't tell if it was model selection or cache churn." — FinSaaS SRE
- "Quantization settings are a black box; show us a sample prompt and the expected diff in outputs if possible." — MedScan product lead
- "We'd take a small drop in quality for predictable latency during business hours." — eCom pilot PM

Prioritized probe lanes (4–6 week horizon)
1) Cache visibility + micro-controls (High impact, Low effort)
   - Deliverable: per-route cache telemetry (hit/miss rate, last-evict time) surfaced in Console + API.
   - Quick patch: add a simple "cache-stats" endpoint for debug (SRE + CS) and a small Console card with three numbers: hit%, recent writes, effective TTL.
   - Rationale: immediate unblock for support and reduces time-to-resolution on cost spikes.

2) Tail-latency small probe: warmup heuristics for long sequences (Medium impact, Medium effort)
   - Deliverable: opt-in runtime flag for "sequence-length-aware prewarm" on a per-route basis; include diagnostics showing warmup efficacy.
   - Experiment: roll to 3 pilot customers (FinSaaS, two internal sandboxes) and measure 95/99p latency shift and token-per-second throughput.

3) Quantization decision playground (High impact, Medium effort)
   - Deliverable: Console sandbox that runs a small prompt set (customer-provided or common evals) across three model variants (base, 8-bit, 4-bit-lite) and returns token latency, cost estimate, and a rough delta-score (BLEU/ROUGE proxy) where applicable.
   - Quick-win: document recommended default for common workloads (chat vs completion vs embeddings).

4) Fallback policy UI + audit trail (Medium impact, Low effort)
   - Deliverable: add a simple policy toggle and explicit log entries when fallback triggers (route->model variant mapping, reason code).
   - Rationale: reduces emergency rollbacks and gives product teams confidence to enable fallbacks.

Low-effort patches (under 1 week)
- Add a CS-facing label in Console for "recent deployment changes" tied to rollout windows (reduces finger-pointing).
- Expose KV cache hit% via the existing metrics API endpoint (no Console work required).
- Small docs refresh: one-pager titled "When latency spikes: checklist for CS/SRE" and a Slack shortcut link for quick escalation.

Customer impact matrix (notes)
- FinSaaS: very latency-sensitive, willing to accept quantized variants during trading hours if SLOs improve.
- MedScan: regulatory constraints; needs audit trail + private deployment compatibility for fallback policies.
- eCom pilot: cost-driven; wants aggressive batching & caching recommendations from Optimize.

Open questions / unknowns
- How much quality regression do real-world prompts see at the 4-bit-lite profile for the Llama-derivative models customers use? (we need a small A/B with labeled prompts)
- Are tail events primarily KV-cache churn, or do they arise from kernel contention under mixed sequence distributions? Need correlation across infra metrics (GPU scheduler) + runtime logs.
- What level of per-route control over TTL/eviction is acceptable from a security/compliance perspective for Private deployments?

Suggested next steps (owners + ETA)
- Ship cache-stats endpoint (SRE + runtime) — owner: Marco Ruiz — ETA: 1 week (2026-08-19).
- Console card for cache hit% (Console team) — owner: Leah Wong — ETA: 2 weeks after endpoint (2026-08-26).
- Define quantization playground scope + sample prompts (Customer Success + Applied ML) — owner: Aisha Patel + Samir Kapoor — ETA: 2 weeks (2026-08-26).
- Kick a small warmup probe (opt-in flag) with two pilot customers — owner: Platform Eng (runbook + telemetry) — ETA: 3 weeks (2026-09-02).

Communication / stakeholder plan
- Quick sync with Product (Optimize, Console) and Applied ML next Monday to prioritize runway for quantization playground.
- Share a 1-page status note to pilot customers with the two-week timeline for cache visibility (reduces churn).
- Link to this doc in the CS triage channel and tag ticket owners for any currently escalated cases.

Appendix: short checklist for support engineers
1) Check cache-stats endpoint -> hit% low? ask for recent sequence length distribution.
2) If 95/99p latency spike and cache hit% < 70%, suggest enabling route TTL bump (pilot).
3) For quantization regression complaints, collect 3 representative prompts and file to CS-quant-eval queue (CS-1142).

Notes to self
- Keep this pocket doc minimal and actionable. If pilots respond positively, fold into a fuller product brief for Sept planning.

---
End of pocket synthesis.
